items.title: Headphone auto-reconnect races boot handshakes: Onn_ connects, shows pairing twice, does not land connected -- per-device isolation on one radio was an early OpenSpan victory and must hold at boot too  [reconnect-race]
items.why: Doug at the 00:48 cold boot: their connections should not be affected by other device handshakes
items.model: Sonnet triage -> Opus fix + Architect review

extra.note: Evidence: app log 00:49:17 bridge READY -> auto-reconnect Onn_; 00:49:21 connected CHECK claimed; lanes iPad/Mac/Laptop ready 00:49:28-29 AFTER; Doug observed connect -> pairing x2 -> not connected. App's claim and reality disagree. Suspects: auto-reconnect fires at bridge-READY while guest lane bring-up still running; guest bluetoothd/agent serialization across controllers; or Windows-side flash before stand-down. Triage is read-only. REFINED (Doug's ears): Pairing -> Connected -> Pairing -> Pairing. It DID land; the 00:49:21 claim was true at claim time; TEARDOWN within seconds, then earbuds kicked into pairing mode x2. Re-ranked to post-connect teardown by what ran after: openspan_bt.py list at 00:49:22 and lane bring-ups landing 00:49:28-29. Second defect: no post-claim monitoring -- the app never noticed the loss. Triage agent updated mid-flight. TRIAGE VERDICT (Sonnet, journal-anchored, high confidence): SELF-INFLICTED SCRIPTED COLLISION, not device contention. btready.sh runs 'systemctl restart openspan-wireplumber' UNCONDITIONALLY every boot; tonight it fired 04:49:22.7 UTC -- 2.1s after Onn_'s A2DP stream landed (fd0 ready 04:49:20.6) -- unregistered the old endpoints (tore the stream), forced AVDTP renegotiation (fd1 04:49:26), then the new wireplumber<->bluetoothd release handshake desynced ('Release doesn't exist' + dbus rejected) leaving the transport dead. Earbuds' pairing-voice x2 = the two renegotiation/failure events. Lane daemons started 1.1s AFTER the damage -- exonerated tonight. SECONDARY (real, latent): iPad BLE lane runs on hci0, the SAME controller as Onn_ A2DP -- isolation principle violated in the radio map; not proximate tonight. THIRD: app has no post-claim monitoring (single 6s D-Bus poll, accurate but unwatched). SSH concurrency + list polls exonerated (read-only, no side effects). Fix options to Doug: (A) end the by-design race -- app's READY edge should not fire until btready.sh has finished its bounce sequence (or make the wireplumber restart conditional on no connected A2DP transport); (B) app-side follow-up transport check 5-8s after the check-mark; (C) radio map -- move iPad BLE off hci0 or 4th dongle (ties to v2.90). CORRECTION (Architect, from DEVLOG ~Jul 6 + multi-radio section): dual-use of one radio (BLE HID + A2DP) is PROVEN, FOUNDATIONAL, and a deliberately supported config -- 'the breakage was never the protocol, it was operational coupling; restarting audio must never touch the keyboard, and vice versa.' The triage's 'isolation violated on hci0' framing was WRONG and option C (move iPad off hci0 / 4th dongle) is WITHDRAWN. Real diagnosis: btready.sh violates the written segregation law twice every boot -- unconditional 'restart bluetooth' (touches every device on every controller) and unconditional 'restart openspan-wireplumber' (tears down live audio). Revised fix awaiting Doug's sign-off: A' = btready.sh law-compliant (bounce sequence completes BEFORE READY fires; wireplumber restart conditional on no live A2DP transport) + B = app re-checks transport 5-8s after the check-mark and retries/reports on loss. Fast-pair precedent is the house style: audio yields the radio by consent and auto-restores, never by bulldozer. SIGNED OFF by Doug 01:0x ('There truly is only one way forward. Yes, AB go'). Opus agent implementing A'+B: btready.sh sequenced+conditional with the Jul-6 law commented in, READY gated on completion marker (with a no-hang timeout), app post-check-mark re-verify with fail-counter respect. Guest changes deploy via the app's own sync at next bridge start; no radio poked by any agent. Proof run: Doug's ears at the next cold boot. IMPLEMENTED+REVIEWED (d173c20, 68db740; ~62k Opus): root finding -- READY was never derived from btready.sh, only from ssh echo; the two components had never heard of each other. Now: btready.sh writes /run/openspan/btready.done from an EXIT trap, both restarts conditional on a2dp_transport_live() (busctl MediaTransport1, bluetoothctl fallback), the Jul-6 law + this incident dated in the script header; app gates READY on marker-or-systemd-state in its own thread, 210s bound, finally-lifts; B re-verifies the TRANSPORT (not the device flag) 7s after the check-mark, retry capped at 3 consecutive teardowns. Tests 58 OK re-verified by Architect. Staged exe rebuilt (carries B + surface mode). DEPLOY: app-side live at exe swap; guest side syncs at next bridge start. PROOF: Doug's ears at the first cold boot after the swap. TEST METHOD RULED by Doug: no variable changes mid-session -- the test follows a computer restart like last time. Hot swap cancelled. Deployed instead by ON-DISK rename-swap 01:2x (running process untouched, 6 procs alive): EsotericOS.exe now sha8 635D9062 (= staged build 01:13, carries fix B + READY gate + surface mode); rollback at EsotericOS.exe.prev. Guest btready.sh fix deploys via the app's own script-sync; NOTE the one-boot lag -- btready.sh runs at guest boot BEFORE the app syncs, so restart #1 boots the OLD guest script (ear symptom may recur once, expected) and deposits the new one; restart #2 is the true A' ear test. App-side B + READY gate are live from restart #1. TRAIN UPDATE after the (unannounced) 01:34 restart: that boot launched the OLD exe (procs 01:36:23+) and the OLD guest btready.sh, but its 01:36-37 script sync deposited the FIXED btready.sh onto the guest. My on-disk swap (01:39) means the NEXT restart launches the NEW exe AND the guest boots the FIXED script -- the one-boot lag was consumed; next restart is the FULL A'+B ear test in one. No ear data from the 01:36 sign-in -- Doug deliberately cased the earbuds rather than test against a corrupted variable set (network mid-recovery, old guest script).
